newsitem.title: USA: Tidewater says O.I.L. acquisition accretive.
newsitem.headline: Tidewater says O.I.L. acquisition accretive.

text.p: Tidewater Inc Chairman William C. O'Malley on Thursday said he expects the company's acquisition of Ocean Group Plc's O.I.L. Ltd subsidiary to add two cents a share to earnings in the first year.
The New Orleans-based energy services firm, which posted $1.23 a share earnings in fiscal 1996, agreed to acquire the Ocean Group unit for 328 million stg, or about $525 million.
The accretion assumes continuation of a share repurchase plan out of free cash flow, O'Malley said.
The company expects international day rates to rise over the next three years to come into line with higher U.S. day rates, boosting cash flow and profits from the acquisition.
The deal will be financed under a $600 million credit facility the company expects to repay out of total cash flow in two to two-and-a-half years, Tidewater executives said.
The acquisition of O.I.L. and its fleet of about 100 vessels allowed Tidewater to add to its market share without increasing the number of vessels in the market, O'Malley said.
Tidewater operates a major fleet of about 650 vessels in the international offshore energy industry, and also rents natural gas compressors in the United States.
